title: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (2019)
summary: Superseded guidance on the diagnosis and pharmacological management of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) in adults. Replaced by MSGC-CHF-2026. Retained for audit of decisions made while it was in force; it must not be presented as current guidance.

recommendations.title: First-line pharmacological treatment for HFrEF
recommendations.text: Offer an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and a beta-blocker licensed for heart failure to adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Titrate each to the maximum tolerated licensed dose before adding a further agent.

recommendations.title: Adding a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
recommendations.text: Consider adding a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) for adults who remain symptomatic on an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker at maximum tolerated doses. Monitor serum potassium and renal function within one week of initiation.

recommendations.title: Renal monitoring on ACE inhibitor therapy
recommendations.text: Measure serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate before starting an ACE inhibitor, one to two weeks after initiation, and after each dose increase.

title: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (2026 update)
summary: Current guidance on the diagnosis and pharmacological management of chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) in adults. This guideline updates and replaces MSGC-CHF-2019. The principal change is the move from sequential two-agent initiation to combined four-pillar therapy started early after diagnosis.

recommendations.title: First-line pharmacological treatment for HFrEF
recommendations.text: Offer all four of the following to adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, started within four weeks of diagnosis rather than sequentially: an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), a beta-blocker licensed for heart failure, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and a sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor. Begin each at a low dose and titrate in parallel. This replaces the sequential ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker approach in MSGC-CHF-2019 recommendation 1.1.1.

recommendations.title: Exception: severe chronic kidney disease
recommendations.text: Recommendation 1.1.1 does not apply unmodified to adults with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 20 ml/min/1.73m2. In this group, do not initiate an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure indication; initiate the remaining three agents and seek specialist renal input before adding a fourth. This is an exception to recommendation 1.1.1, not a separate pathway.

recommendations.title: Exception: symptomatic hypotension
recommendations.text: Where systolic blood pressure is persistently below 100 mmHg, stagger initiation of the agents in recommendation 1.1.1 rather than starting them together, prioritising the beta-blocker and the SGLT2 inhibitor, which have the least blood-pressure-lowering effect at initiation. This is an exception to the parallel-initiation instruction in recommendation 1.1.1.

recommendations.title: Renal monitoring on four-pillar therapy
recommendations.text: Measure serum creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate and serum potassium before initiation, at one to two weeks after starting therapy, and after each dose increase. An early fall in eGFR of up to 30 percent after SGLT2 inhibitor initiation is expected and is not on its own a reason to stop treatment.

title: Atrial fibrillation: stroke prevention and anticoagulation (2024)
summary: Current guidance on assessing stroke risk and offering anticoagulation to adults with atrial fibrillation.

recommendations.title: Offering anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation
recommendations.text: Offer anticoagulation with a direct-acting oral anticoagulant (DOAC) to adults with atrial fibrillation and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 2 or above, after discussing the benefits and bleeding risk. Do not use aspirin monotherapy for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation.

recommendations.title: Exception: mechanical heart valve or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis
recommendations.text: Recommendation 2.1.1 does not apply to adults with a mechanical heart valve or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis. Offer a vitamin K antagonist with target INR monitoring instead; direct-acting oral anticoagulants are not indicated in this group. This is an exception to recommendation 2.1.1.

title: Type 2 diabetes in adults: glycaemic targets (2021)
summary: Withdrawn guidance on glycaemic targets in adults with type 2 diabetes. Withdrawn on 2025-11-30 following safety review; no replacement guideline has been issued. Must not be used to inform current care.

recommendations.title: HbA1c target for adults on a single agent
recommendations.text: Support adults with type 2 diabetes managed by a single glucose-lowering agent to aim for an HbA1c of 48 mmol/mol (6.5 percent). This recommendation is withdrawn and must not be applied.
